items.title: Advances in Agentic Computer Graphics
items.reason_zh: 图形学 Agent 与文献系统的一般综述，反馈主要用于生成和修订图形代码产物；摘要未提出 Harness 演化专项方法、理论或评测。

evidence_quotes.quote: Computer graphics is built on code. Large language model (LLM) agents can now generate graphics code and iteratively refine it through various feedback. This capability opens the door to a potentially new paradigm of computer graphics, with graphics algorithms increasingly built around agentic systems to automate progressively complex tasks. Over the past years, research on agentic graphics has expanded rapidly across a diverse range of tasks. This rapid growth makes it increasingly difficult for manual literature reviews to keep pace with new developments. At the same time, similar ideas are often described using different terminology across these tasks, further complicating efforts to develop a systematic understanding of the field. In this report, we address these challenges through two contributions. First, we introduce a unified taxonomy for characterizing agentic systems across diverse computer graphics tasks. Second, we develop an agentic literature system that can assist human researchers in analyzing existing and newly published papers at scale. Building on these contributions, we analyze emerging research trends and discuss open challenges in coordinating agents and tools across graphics tasks, designing interfaces and representations for human-agent collaboration, sustaining long-horizon planning and refinement, and reliably evaluating interactive graphics systems.

items.title: Wave Forcing: Towards Speed-of-Light Streaming Video Generation
items.reason_zh: 联合设计视频生成训练与固定并行运行时，优化视频模型和执行效率；没有提出运行程序经反馈自改并跨任务继承。

evidence_quotes.quote: Real-time long-video generation requires continuous output with consistent appearance and natural motion. Existing chunk-wise autoregressive methods face challenges in both generation efficiency and long-video quality: serialized denoising and history-cache refresh require two forward passes even with one-step denoising, and longer rollouts can degrade quality and cause camera drift. We propose Wave Forcing (WF), which co-designs generation, training, and execution for continuous video output with multi-step denoising. WF uses chunk-wise causal attention to access earlier, cleaner chunks before their denoising is complete, and distributes staggered denoising and cache-refresh stages across full-model replicas to achieve 1F1C: one output chunk per concurrent forward round after pipeline fill. To adapt the model to this continuous generation process, we develop a three-stage training procedure that successively introduces mixed-noise denoising, motion supervision, and causal adaptation using self-generated history. To execute this process efficiently, Wave Runtime (WaveRT) uses Wave Parallelism (WP) for early K/V delivery and communication-computation overlap, together with optimized kernels and pipelined VAE decoding. Experiments on Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B show that 5-step WF maintains overall quality comparable to Rolling Forcing while achieving higher Dynamic Degree on both short and long videos. Our system efficiency experiments show that 4-step WF achieves 147.6 DiT FPS and 134.8 end-to-end FPS on eight H200 GPUs, yielding 7.07x the single-GPU end-to-end throughput. In DiT-only tests with matched SageAttention+W8A8 backends, denoising steps, and GPU counts, WP delivers up to 2.53x the throughput of the faster of the Ulysses and Ring context-parallel baselines across six model scales (1.3B-14B).

items.title: CUA-Master: Scaling Computer-use Agents through Open-World Recursive Improvements

evidence_quotes.quote: As illustrated by the black dashed box in Figure 2(a) , we formulate our methodology as a recursive flywheel driven by two complementary forces. Open-world seeding (Section 2.3 ) continuously injects real-world diversity and operational knowledge by discovering underrepresented applications, operations, and workflows, mitigating the risks of closed-loop degeneration associated with purely self-generated data [ 11 , 43 , 73 ] . Autocatalytic propagation (Section 2.4 ) transforms these real-world seeds into reusable primitives, enabling composable task synthesis and reliable trajectory collection in executable environments. Together, these two forces establish a self-reinforcing cycle in which open-world seeding provides external knowledge and diversity and forms the necessary foundation, while autocatalytic propagation systematically amplifies its coverage, complexity, and scale.

where n n denotes the number of generated primitives, each of which is a five-tuple comprising the associated application u u , the reusable ability a a , execution preconditions 𝒫 \mathcal{P} , environment requirements ℰ \mathcal{E} , and verifier specification 𝒱 \mathcal{V} , to formulate the operational dependencies required for execution and verification. Here, we follow and further improve the strategies from [ 52 , 28 ] to automatically build corresponding ℰ \mathcal{E} and 𝒱 \mathcal{V} for each primitive.
We aggregate the extracted primitives into an application-indexed primitive library ℬ \mathcal{B} . Semantically equivalent primitives are canonicalized and deduplicated, while variants with distinct preconditions, environment requirements, or verification logic are retained. This representation aims to abstract away task-specific entities while preserving the operational dependencies necessary for reliable execution, enabling a primitive to be instantiated with different files, content, interface states, and application configurations.

As capability gains from SFT gradually saturate, we transition to RL in the final iteration to further enhance the task-level capability upper limit. As discussed, the synthesized tasks are built upon controllable capability primitives, which renders native support for difficulty-level categorization. Combining this with task generation quality and rollout success rates, we curate a high-quality task collection for RL training.

evidence_quotes.quote: Agent intelligence is advancing toward lifelong autonomy systems that continually interact and evolve with real-world environments. Progress toward Artificial Super Intelligence (ASI) requires attention to both model capability and the runtime systems that translate reasoning into action. Ideally, such agents would invoke tools, interpret feedback, maintain working state, and continue when their immediate interaction ends. To achieve this, the agent harness supplies the runtime mechanisms for this process, including tool orchestration, state and context management, and execution feedback. Because the harness shapes how a model acts and how well it can use available resources, models and their harnesses need to co-evolve ( Liu et al., 2024 ; Sumers et al., 2024 ) .
CoworkOS organizes experiments and analysis. GLM-5.3 primarily serves as the controller and data teacher, while Qwen3.6-35B-A3B is the model trained and evaluated.
Across five rounds, CoworkOS continually uses evaluation feedback to identify capabilities to strengthen, revise the data recipe, and update the training strategy.

evidence_quotes.quote: Robot-use Agents (RUAs) have shown promising zero-shot manipulation capabilities, but reliance on frontier, proprietary models limits research into further training. To democratize RUA research, we introduce uni-robot-agent, a unified harness for competitive open-weight robot use that supports further training. Without privileged inputs, an out-of-the-box Qwen3.8-Flash-Next achieves a RoboDojo Score of 31.39, surpassing the published GPT-6 Astra-RoboProbe result of 28.97 and many VLA/WAM baselines, and performs competitively on 19 real-world tasks. Our analysis across model generations, families, and sizes links effective robot use to four general capabilities, suggesting that future RUA training should develop them jointly.

evidence_quotes.quote:
SWE-Trail applies a narrower form of adaptive allocation within one issue.
The history of that issue is compiled before the new collection round, and the
resulting rules remain fixed during the rollout. They guide where additional
collection effort is spent and how executed alternatives are compared, without
changing the coding-agent prompt, tools, or model weights.

Before collection begins, the compiler validates each proposed detector state against its supporting evidence and replays its rules on the recorded attempts. States without sufficient support are discarded. The admitted detector states, their comparison objectives, and λ i \lambda_{i} are then fixed for the entire collection round. Appendices B and F.5 provide the compiler details, admission checks, and example records.

Limitations and future work. Our experiments use two student models but one collection model and one agent scaffold. Future work could test other collection models and scaffolds. Our current setting also keeps history fixed during each collection round and uses the same collection budget for every issue. Future work could update history across rounds and allocate effort differently across issues. The exploratory replay audit in Appendix G.1 also motivates testing more diverse candidate proposals. Extending SWE-Trail beyond coding would require environments that support state restoration and feedback for comparing alternatives. Web navigation is one possible direction.

items.title: PhotoGuider: Composition-Aware Cropping and 360^{circ} View Framing with Explainable Photographic Assessments
items.reason_zh: 研究图像裁剪、全景取景与解释的学习型评分器，改进对象为视觉模型及图片产物。

evidence_quotes.quote: Traditional image cropping assumes the photograph already contains the composition worth keeping, and asks only where to crop. A full 360^{circ} scene offers no such guarantee: the viewing direction in a scene has to be discovered before anything can be framed. We present PhotoGuider, a measure-then-frame method that answers both questions with compact learned scorers over one shared set of composition-aware features. The designed features are extracted using foundation and task-specific vision models and structured into four photographic tokens: Subject, Composition, Aesthetics, and Integrity. Our MLLM explainer is fine-tuned to generate composition-related explanations conditioned on images and measured token assessments. To our knowledge, PhotoGuider is the first method to combine explicit composition-based direction selection in 360^{circ} panoramas with refined framing, camera-parameter output for native re-rendering, and measurement-conditioned explanations. On two standard 2D cropping benchmarks, PhotoGuider achieves the highest average mIoU performance against ground-truth crops. In a blind ranking study, 120 participants ranked three cropping methods over 100 panoramic scenes from the public Poly Haven HDRI library, placing our framings first in 53.2% of cases, against 27.3% and 19.5% for two strong alternatives. Project page: https://ntuneillee.github.io/research/photoguider/

items.title: Lost in Recovery: Demystifying Recovery Behavior of Computer-Use Agents via Goal-Oriented Action Replay
items.reason_zh: ReTrace评测执行中的故障恢复能力，属于一般Computer-use可靠性评测；摘要没有把Harness版本演化作为研究对象。

evidence_quotes.quote: Recent advances in large (vision) language models have enabled computer-use agents that automate digital workflows via fine-grained keyboard and mouse operations. However, such agents remain fragile in long-horizon settings, where errors accumulate and executed actions leave unintended side effects, making the ability to recover from failures critical. Yet, existing remedies remain inadequate: environment resets are infeasible in proprietary settings, action replay is prohibitively expensive over long horizons, and API-based rollback is limited to web environments, leaving model-based recovery largely unexplored. To address this gap, we present ReTrace, a scalable evaluation framework for systematically studying recovery behavior in computer-use agents. We formalize Transition-Consistent Recovery: identical downstream actions from the recovered and target states must yield identical outcomes. We operationalize this criterion through goal-oriented action replay following controlled error injection. Using ReTrace, we present the first systematic study of autonomous, model-based recovery, revealing that (i) ideal recovery can unlock model's latent task completion capabilities, (ii) current computer-use agents fail to exploit their latent recovery capabilities, and (iii) accurate model-based recovery yields measurable end-to-end gains. Together, these findings establish recovery as a fundamental capability for building reliable computer-use agents. Our code and dataset is available at https://github.com/BangProx/ReTRACE.

items.title: IdeaTaste: Do LLMs Share the Research Taste of Human Researchers?
items.reason_zh: 比较AI科研提案与人类后续研究的选题品味，属于AI研发能力评测，非Harness演化专项。

evidence_quotes.quote: Research taste, the judgment of what to read, which problems to pursue, and which methods to try, increasingly shapes the work of AI scientists, yet it remains far less understood than their ability to execute research. We introduce IdeaTaste, a benchmark that scores an LLM by how closely the research proposals it writes from a literature snapshot frozen at 2025 match the work the same communities published in 2026. Our experiments span six contemporary language models and four research areas from established to emerging fields, covering more than 90{,}000 proposals in total. LLM agents fall well short of human communities in both the literature they cite and the ideas they state, reaching about 26\% of the human level on citation matching and only 18\% on idea matching. Their populations can cite as diversely as a community and take up its tasks and methods, yet rarely arrive at the concrete approaches and research plans it pursues. Neither richer field context nor larger populations substantially close this gap. In blinded expert review, AI proposals trail the 2026 papers least in presentation and most in expected success, echoing their gap in concrete approaches, and those whose ideas no human paper shares fare worst, suggesting weaker directions rather than overlooked opportunities. These results indicate that the main bottleneck in AI research taste lies less in finding the directions a community works on than in turning them into the concrete approaches it goes on to pursue. We release IdeaTaste as an open, continuously updated leaderboard (https://cxcscmu.github.io/IdeaTaste) that benchmarks contemporary AI proposals against future publication cycles.

items.title: Order-Only On-Policy Distillation
items.reason_zh: 通过教师token排序训练学生模型，直接优化权重与蒸馏目标。

evidence_quotes.quote: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student on its own generations by matching the teacher's token probabilities. These probabilities entangle two kinds of information: which tokens the teacher prefers, and how confident it is. The latter reflects the teacher's own capacity and calibration, which a smaller student may be unable to reproduce. Because the teacher temperature changes these values without changing the ordering, OPD is also sensitive to the temperature choice. We ask whether the teacher's ordering of candidate tokens is enough, and propose Order-Only On-Policy Distillation (O^{3}PD). At each student-generated prefix, O^{3}PD trains the student to reproduce the order of the teacher's top-K tokens, without fitting their probability values. The objective is therefore invariant to the teacher temperature and needs no temperature tuning. Across six teacher--student pairs, O^{3}PD outperforms OPD on the average over HMMT25, AIME24, and AIME25 in every pair, by up to 2.9 points, with gains of up to 5.6 points on AIME25. Other ranking losses yield similar gains, so the benefit comes from ordinal supervision itself. Analysis shows that O^{3}PD departs further from the teacher's probabilities than OPD, yet reproduces its ranking more faithfully and yields a stronger student. The ranking, not the probability values, thus carries the knowledge that on-policy distillation needs to transfer.

items.title: Reviso: Not All Visual Evidence Deserves Equal Attention in Video Captioning
items.reason_zh: 验证与教师修订用于生成训练轨迹，GRPO训练观察策略；对当前视频改计划是任务内推理，未展示外部程序反馈修订后跨任务保留。

evidence_quotes.quote: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can generate detailed video captions, yet they may overemphasize minor details while overlooking essential context and key events. We argue that not all visual evidence deserves equal attention, as the importance of visual information depends on the content of each video. Motivated by this observation, we propose Reviso, an agentic video captioning framework that learns what to observe and how to gather relevant visual evidence. From a low-frame-rate global preview, Reviso constructs a hierarchical Context--Focus--Points (CFP) observation plan that identifies the video context, prioritizes key aspects, and defines concrete observation targets and corresponding tools. Guided by this plan, Reviso performs goal-directed active perception by selectively revisiting temporal segments and combining tools for fine-grained inspection. It interprets the acquired evidence, updates its plan as needed, and integrates global and local information to generate the final caption. To learn this observation strategy, we develop a verification-guided pipeline that constructs high-quality training trajectories through factual verification and teacher-guided refinement. We further train Reviso using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), incorporating a key-fact reward for caption quality, a Plan Alignment Reward (PAR) for identifying important observation targets, and an Unproductive Tool-Call Penalty (UTCP) that adjusts observation-cost penalties based on caption quality. Experiments across four video captioning benchmarks show that Reviso outperforms the evaluated open-source baselines, while its generated captions better support downstream video question answering. These findings highlight the effectiveness and potential of priority-guided active observation for video captioning.

items.title: From Fragmentation to Fusion: A Survey and Roadmap for Omnimodal Embeddings
items.reason_zh: 多模态嵌入表征的综述和立场，研究对象是表征覆盖、对齐与组合性。

evidence_quotes.quote: Embedding models underpin virtually every modern AI system, from search engines to recommendation systems. Despite shared mathematical foundations, research on embedding models remains fragmented by modality: the communities develop largely in isolation, seldom exchanging insights. We argue that this fragmentation obscures a deeper convergence. Driven by contrastive learning, Transformer architectures, and a granularity shift, embedding research across modalities is converging toward a common set of principles, even as modality-specific challenges remain underexplored. To reason across this convergence without conflating it, we propose a framework of three progressively harder capabilities: coverage, comparability, and compositionality. Three paths toward unification satisfy these in turn: transformation broadens coverage, alignment enables comparability, and joint embedding, the terminus we advocate, aims at compositionality. This position paper traces the resulting evolution, providing the first unified, cross-cutting treatment of omnimodal embedding research.

items.title: When Does Latent Prediction Error Support Physical Surprise Claims in Video World Models?
items.reason_zh: 评估视频世界模型表征及预测误差能否测量物理惊讶，非Harness程序演化理论或评测。

evidence_quotes.quote: Prediction errors from video world models are often treated as physical surprise, but they can also reflect appearance, static content, motion, or ordinary prediction difficulty. We present an evaluation framework that separates what frozen representations contain, how they organize appearance and physical differences, and what changes a model's own prediction error. On IntPhys2, a benchmark of physically possible and impossible events, we compare representations from latent prediction, masked pixel reconstruction, and simple visual statistics. Appearance remains easy to decode, while V-JEPA2 exposes modest information about whether events are possible or impossible. Looking at the latent geometry, appearance changes become smaller compared with differences between videos, their directions line up more consistently across scenes, and their overlap with physical changes decreases in deeper layers. Across action-conditioned models, incorrect actions raise prediction error, while appearance changes also produce substantial responses. In Physion++ video clips, repeating a single frame can produce higher error than the original clip, while changing color throughout the clip can lower it. Using Kubric, a simulation and rendering framework, we find that impossible events can produce lower error than possible events. A fixed error threshold also incorrectly flags many possible events as impossible. A model can therefore represent physical information and respond to incorrect actions without its native prediction error reliably measuring physical surprise.

items.title: CrossSWE: Benchmarking Cross-Repository Joint Development for Coding Agents

evidence_quotes.quote: As coding agents achieve increasingly high success rates on software engineering benchmarks, recent efforts have sought to increase task complexity through longer horizons and more extensive code modifications. However, real-world software development often spans multiple interdependent repositories, introducing additional challenges in dependency reasoning, change propagation, and interface consistency. Rather than further increasing complexity within individual repositories, we introduce CrossSWE, a benchmark for cross-repository joint development comprising 171 real-world instances spanning 165 repositories, 20 technical domains, and 13 programming languages. CrossSWE verifies the necessity of coordinated changes by testing whether partial repository modifications are insufficient to achieve the intended behavior. Our evaluation of five LLMs reveals substantial challenges, with the strongest model, GPT-6.1 Sol, achieving only 58.48% Pass@1. Furthermore, cross-repository inconsistencies emerge as the most prevalent failure mode (44.2%), highlighting the difficulty of maintaining consistency across interdependent repositories.

items.title: Diagnosing the Reference Gap: What Visual Scaffolds Can and Cannot Fix in Multimodal Reasoning
items.reason_zh: 固定视觉编号等外部参照的配对消融评测；training-free视觉技能并不自动意味着技能按反馈迭代和继承。

evidence_quotes.quote: Multimodal large language models can recognize visual content yet struggle to reason reliably over it across multiple steps. In counting, a model may see all objects but lose track of which ones it has counted. We argue that such failures, commonly attributed to perception, reveal a reference gap: the failure to bind language to the relevant visual entities, regions, or locations. Motivated by the theory of visual routines, we test whether external references such as numbering can narrow this gap. We introduce ReGap-Bench, a paired benchmark of five visual reasoning tasks in which the scene, question, and answer are fixed and only the reference varies. Results show that task-matched references improve accuracy by up to 25\%, while mismatched references provide little benefit or even hurt performance. These findings identify the reference gap as a bottleneck distinct from visual perception and show that constructing task-appropriate visual references can serve as a training-free visual skill for improving multimodal reasoning.

items.title: FLAMIA: FLAsh MIcroscaling Attention for Fast and Causally Safe Training on Blackwell
items.reason_zh: 提出Blackwell注意力训练kernel与量化调度设计，优化对象是模型训练的算子实现。

evidence_quotes.quote: Attention remains a substantial computational cost in Transformer training, particularly at long context lengths. NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs provide high-throughput low-precision matrix multiplication, but exploiting it in attention requires addressing quantization overhead, causal information leakage through shared scales, and numerical inconsistencies between the forward and backward passes. We present FLAMIA, a family of attention kernels for Blackwell with MXFP8 and mixed NVFP4/FP8 training paths. Our design combines token-block scaling that reuses quantized operands across matrix orientations, targeted safeguards against scale-induced leakage, and consistent forward and backward computations. Fused quantization and architecture-specific kernel optimizations reduce overhead, while document-local scaling and workload-aware scheduling support variable-length documents directly in packed layouts without repacking. Across various causal packed-document workloads, the MXFP8 path accelerates the combined forward and backward attention call, including quantization, by factors of 1.10--1.40times on B200 and 1.06--1.42times on B300 relative to the fastest evaluated baseline for each workload. We validate training stability and quality preservation on pretraining Llama-style models. These results show how jointly designing quantization, training numerics, and document scheduling translates low-bit hardware throughput into practical attention acceleration.

items.title: Avatar Intelligence: Amplifying Human Agency Through Persistent Personal Agents
items.reason_zh: 第4.2节明确提出跨episode的用户情境Rehearsal Engineering，更新记忆、技能选择和决策策略，不能说它没有反馈演化；全文主题仍是个人Agent个性化、授权与监督的一般议程，不是Harness演化专项。建议留为通用RSI相关理论。

evidence_quotes.quote: The engineering of autonomous agents has historically focused on improving intent understanding and task completion through external scaffolding. From this perspective, prompt engineering injects user intent and constraints into the instruction channel; context engineering injects situational state (documents, observations, and memory) to ground planning; and harness engineering injects executable rules and control policies (e.g., tool gating, verification, retries, and escalation) to stabilize the action loop. These paradigms primarily shape behavior at inference time by conditioning what the agent sees and what it is allowed to do.

For Avatar Intelligence, feedback cannot remain purely generic. Beyond learning in standardized benchmarks or public web contexts, an avatar must specialize within the user's own ecology: their tools, routines, constraints, and risk tolerances.
We refer to this user-situated specialization loop as Rehearsal Engineering : a system-level methodology for aligning a standardized, language-trained agent to the user's real environment by (1) collecting user- and environment-specific traces and preferences, (2) staging representative scenarios (via simulation, counterfactual rollouts, or controlled sandboxing), (3) evaluating candidate actions with explicit oversight policies, and (4) updating the avatar's memory, skill selection, and decision policy under bounded autonomy.

evidence_quotes.quote: Decision models target structured tasks by directly predicting choices or scores, avoiding autoregressive decoding latency. However, transferring a generative LLM's ranking knowledge to a decision model remains challenging: the teacher expresses preferences through a ranked list of document ID sequences, while the student determines the ranking using scores from the first-token position. To bridge this gap, we introduce DecisionRank, a decision model trained through item-space on-policy distillation (OPD). Item-space OPD constructs the student's rollout by sorting its document scores into a ranked sequence. A generative teacher takes the resulting ranking list as inputs and provides conditional feedback to directly supervise those scores. Combined with offline ranking supervision, DecisionRank achieves state-of-the-art performance on both general and reasoning-intensive retrieval benchmarks such as TREC DL, BEIR, and BRIGHT. Across four benchmarks, item-space OPD consistently outperforms alternative training objectives. Even at 1.7B parameters, DecisionRank surpasses its 27B generative teacher on TREC DL19--23. At 8B, it outperforms its generative listwise counterpart while running 24.5times faster on TREC DL and 16.7times faster on BRIGHT.

items.title: Measuring AI Agents as Teammates with Collaborative Intelligence
items.reason_zh: 评测AI作为团队成员的协作能力，虽有留出任务但不是Harness版本演化的专项基准。

evidence_quotes.quote: Progress in AI is often measured by what a single model can do on its own. Yet teams of AI agents are starting to make breakthroughs and discoveries in science, medicine, mathematics and software engineering. As AI begins to work in teams of agents and people, the ability to collaborate becomes a core part of their intelligence. Research on human teams has measured this ability for decades. Inspired by this, we introduce the Collaborative Intelligence Benchmark, which measures how well an AI agent works as a teammate. It contains 240 tasks across 8 dimensions of teamwork, from refusing an unsafe shortcut to checking the work that a weaker model leaves behind. Each task comes from a real record or an existing benchmark, from aviation accident reports and clinical cases to coding tasks and negotiations, and has a programmatically verifiable outcome. To isolate teamwork from individual capability, models are scored only on tasks that they can solve by themselves when they have full information. We evaluate 18 closed- and open-weight models and find that every model, across sizes and families, has clear weaknesses as a teammate, with the best model scoring only 82.2 out of 100. Frontier models almost always refuse unsafe shortcuts and report misconduct, yet they cave under interpersonal pressure, reaching the best overall deal in only 14% of conflicts, and their pass rate drops from 97% to 81% when they take over a task in which a weaker model has cheated. Crucially, general capability does not guarantee good teamwork, as models with nearly the same capability score differ by up to 11 points as teammates. The benchmark includes 160 public tasks with code and data, along with 80 held-out tasks for evaluation. As AI agents increasingly work alongside other agents and people, the ability to collaborate effectively is becoming a crucial capability to measure and develop.
